text.content:
This pocket of the Larders should be a rest stop and mostly is, except for the faint sour tang in the air that gets worse the longer anyone stands still. Behind an overturned crate, someone is very obviously trying not to be noticed - and failing, on account of being enormous.

GM Notes

Hazard: A residual effect lingers here, growing worse the longer anyone stays without taking precautions (DC 11 to resist each round) - a lingering fume from whatever spoiled in the Larders' old storage. Nothing that can't be solved by just not loitering.

Subquest - The Other Corvin: The crate hides a friendly Dragonborn barbarian who introduces himself, apologetically, as Corvin Blackwell - "not that Corvin Blackwell, believe me, I get this constantly." He wandered in months ago attached to a passing caravan and has, through no effort of his own, become a minor folk hero to goblins who keep confusing him for their tyrant king by name alone. He's hiding here specifically because a patrol just went through hunting "Corvin Blackwell" and he'd rather not litigate the coincidence again. He's a genuinely useful ally: he knows the warren's rough layout, confirms that "the King" and the drover are the same increasingly-not-goblin person, and will happily impersonate or disambiguate himself in front of goblins if it helps the party get past a checkpoint. He won't join the final fight (wrong Corvin, wrong scale of problem) but will gladly wait here and cheer.
